scenes.text: One of the most famous fossils on Earth is named after a Beatles song.
On November twenty fourth, nineteen seventy four, Donald Johanson and Tom Gray were searching for fossils at Hadar, in Ethiopia.
Taking a different route back, Johanson spotted a small forearm bone in a gully, then ribs, a pelvis and more.
That night, the team celebrated while Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds played over and over.
So the skeleton got the name Lucy.
She belonged to a species called Australopithecus afarensis.
And she lived about three point two million years ago.
Forty seven bones were found, about forty percent of one skeleton.
In life, she stood only about three and a half feet tall.
Her brain was small, but her knee and pelvis show she walked upright on two legs.
That helped settle a big debate: walking upright came before big brains.
The real Lucy is kept safe at the National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa.
What song would you name a famous discovery after?

title: The famous fossil named after a Beatles song 🦴
caption: Lucy was found at Hadar, Ethiopia on Nov 24, 1974. She lived about 3.2 million years ago, and her bones show she walked on two legs.
